name: Ben Gurion International
_magVarNote: Degrees EAST. Retained for reference only. Runway bearings are no longer derived from designator plus variation - they are measured from the real threshold coordinates below, which differ from the derived values by 3 to 6 degrees.

runways.note: Shortest and least active runway - mainly cargo and charter traffic.

typicalPattern._note: Fallback only, used when live traffic is too thin to read (quiet hours, or every ADS-B source down). From Moti Kaplan's post: departures are mostly runway 26; the landing runway tracks the time of day because aircraft land into the wind. Live observation always overrides this.

landingByLocalHour.label: night - no published pattern, live data only

_geometrySource: Threshold coordinates and lengths from OpenStreetMap (Overpass, aeroway=runway around LLBG), combining each runway's centre way with its displaced-threshold ways to get the full paved extent. Computed lengths agree with OSM's own length tags to within 7 m.

diagramProjection._note: Maps lat/lon into the runway diagram's coordinate space. The frame is wider than the airport so approach and departure arrows, and spots a few kilometres out, have somewhere to go.
